nodes.description:
A reproducible genome-wide DNA-methylation pattern in peripheral blood, distinct from the Floating-Harbor signature and from controls.
It is included as a pathophysiology node rather than only as a laboratory test because it is the evidence that DEHMBA is a separate entity. A classifier trained on the FLHS signature calls every DEHMBA case negative, and a signature specific to the proximal-variant group emerges when the comparison is made against controls. A shared spectrum would not do that.

nodes.description:
Satb2 - itself the gene of a distinct neurodevelopmental disorder - is expressed at reduced levels because H2A.Z occupancy at its promoter falls.
This node is mouse-only, and the entry is explicit about that. It is retained rather than dropped because it is the one branch of the mechanism with interventional support: restoring Satb2 rescues the model phenotype, which is a stronger form of evidence than correlation, and it is simultaneously the branch whose translation to human DEHMBA is unproven.

nodes.description: Reduced SRCAP dosage leaves the SRCAP chromatin-remodelling complex - the human counterpart of yeast SWR1 - operating below its normal capacity. The complex's defining job is ATP-dependent exchange of canonical H2A for the histone variant H2A.Z, so a shortfall here is a shortfall in H2A.Z deposition rather than a general chromatin defect.

evidence.reference_title: The ATPase SRCAP is associated with the mitotic apparatus, uncovering novel molecular aspects of Floating-Harbor syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The main function of the SRCAP complex is to promote the exchange of histone H2A with the H2A.Z variant.

nodes.description:
A de novo heterozygous variant in SRCAP that destroys the allele - nonsense, frameshift, canonical or deep-intronic splice-altering, or a retrotransposon insertion - and lies proximal or distal to exons 33-34.
The location is the whole point. A truncation inside exons 33-34 escapes nonsense-mediated decay and yields a stable shortened protein, which is Floating-Harbor syndrome; anywhere else the transcript is degraded and the cell is simply short of SRCAP. So a curator or laboratory reading a novel SRCAP truncation should ask where it sits before predicting which disease it causes, and should not treat DEHMBA as a milder or severer FLHS.
